note:
⛔ SNG-474. HEALING INTENT. CCode measured it: 57 abilities heal, 27 carry dice, and NOT ONE NUMBER IS READ. `mechanic.dice` reaches skill_battle.js:798 guarded on `shape === 'damage'`; outside combat health comes from `rules.recovery` flat values, `ladder.js` grants and `encounters.js` deltas. ⚠️ FOURTH WRITER-WITH-NO-READER after narrationHints, rivals and offscreenVerbs.
⛔ ERIK 2026-08-16: 'I don't care HOW healing is implemented as long as it is good coding practice and works. CCODE can decide how. YOU CAN AUTHOR THE INTENT.' This file is the intent.

whatHealingMustDo.1_scale: ⛔ A HEAL'S SIZE COMES FROM ITS DICE, THE SAME WAY A BLOW'S DOES. 1d4 is a field dressing, 2d4 gets someone back on their feet, 3d4–4d4 is a working surgery, 3d6 is a life pulled back. ⚠️ The 27 authored numbers already express a considered ladder and should not be flattened to a constant.
whatHealingMustDo.2_ranksScaleIt: ⚠️ Physician's Tome is the model: r1 SMALL heal on top of the diagnosis, r2 BIG heal — they get up and can fight today, r3 FULL heal. ⛔ Erik's ruling: 'HEALED IS HEALED' — the rank gain is a QUANTITY, not a duration or a permanence.
whatHealingMustDo.3_inContestAndOut: ⛔ HEALING MUST WORK IN BOTH PLACES AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT. In a contest it is an action spent not attacking — its value is tempo-negative and that is the trade. Out of contest it is the difference between travelling tomorrow and travelling next week. ⚠️ THE SAME NUMBER SHOULD MEAN SOMETHING IN BOTH.
whatHealingMustDo.4_notSymmetricWithDamage: ⚠️ A heal is NOT a negative hit. Line 879's affinity absorb is damage arithmetic inverted, which is correct for what it models and wrong as a general heal: ⛔ A HEAL CANNOT CRIT INTO OVERHEALING AND CANNOT BE EVADED. ⚠️ BUT SEE §5 — IT CAN BE SOAKED, BY THE RIGHT THINGS.
whatHealingMustDo.5_healingCanBeSoaked:
⛔ ERIK 2026-08-16: 'Seems like some BLEEDING, WOUNDING or DEATH skills should also SOAK HEALING.' ⚠️ HE IS RIGHT AND MY 'NOBODY ARMOURS AGAINST BEING MENDED' WAS TOO NEAT — armour does not resist a heal, but A WOUND THAT IS BEING HELD OPEN DOES.
⛔ SO HEALING HAS A SOAK TERM, AND IT IS NOT THE TARGET'S ARMOUR — IT IS THE ACTIVE HARM STILL WORKING ON THEM. That makes anti-healing a real tactical position rather than a status flag.
⚠️ WHAT SHOULD SOAK A HEAL:
   BLEEDING — a wound still open. The heal must first cover what is still being lost.
   HASTENED DECAY — Ashwarden work: 'a wound already open goes grey and stops closing'. ⛔ THAT CRAFT'S WHOLE CLAIM IS THAT MENDING FAILS, and today it is a flavour line.
   SUSTAINED HOLDS — Sustained Regard r2: 'they cannot rally, cannot steady, CANNOT STOP BLEEDING, for as long as you hold it'. ⛔ ALREADY AUTHORED AS ANTI-HEALING AND ALREADY UNREAD.
   ROT, VENOM, CURSE — anything whose fiction is ongoing harm rather than a past injury.
⛔ THE RULE: A HEAL IS REDUCED BY ACTIVE ONGOING HARM, NEVER BY ARMOUR OR EVASION. ⚠️ And a heal that ends the ongoing harm first — Physician's Tome's 'name what is ACTUALLY wrong' — should be able to spend its whole value doing that instead, which is the counter-counter.

boundsThatMatter: ⛔ A heal restores; it does not regrow what is gone. Every healing craft in the corpus already says so.
⚠️ Healing the same subject repeatedly in one contest should return less each time, or a party with one healer never loses.
⛔ The healer must reach the subject. This is the one thing that makes a healer a positioning problem rather than a button.
⚠️ Traditions differ in WHAT they mend: Life regrows, Order repairs to spec, Death holds a thing where it is, Mind corrects the fault.
⛔ Some crafts exist to make healing fail. They must actually make it fail, not merely say so — Hastened Grey and Sustained Regard r2 both already claim it in prose.
forCCode:

Erik: good coding practice, and it works. ⚠️ Two shapes I can see from the content side, neither prescriptive: (a) widen the 798 guard to any shape whose operative axis is restorative and invert the sign — cheapest, reuses tested arithmetic, but inherits crit/evade/soak unless suppressed; (b) a separate resolveHeal path — more code, but the four asymmetries above are stated once instead of suppressed three times.
